title: Connectors
subtitle: Link your ideas smoothly: addition, contrast, reason, and result.
objectives: Use connectors of addition (also, as well as)
Use connectors of contrast (but, however, although)
Use connectors of reason and result (because, so, therefore)

content.intro: You already know "and," "but," and "or." This lesson expands your set of connecting words, organized by what job each one does.

rules.heading: Addition
rules.body: and, also, too, as well as, moreover, furthermore — add a similar idea.

rules.heading: Contrast
rules.body: but, however, although, though, whereas, on the other hand — show a difference or surprise.

rules.heading: Reason & Result
rules.body: because/since/as (reason) → so/therefore (result). "Because" gives the cause; "so" gives the effect.

examples: I like coffee, but I don't like tea.
She studied hard, so she passed the exam.
He is tired, and he wants to rest.
Although it was raining, we went for a walk.
I stayed home because I was sick.
She's very talented; however, she doesn't have much experience.

commonMistakes.wrong: I like coffee, so I don't like tea.
commonMistakes.right: I like coffee, but I don't like tea.
commonMistakes.why: "So" shows result, not contrast — a contrast between two preferences needs "but."

commonMistakes.wrong: She studied hard, but she passed the exam.
commonMistakes.right: She studied hard, so she passed the exam.
commonMistakes.why: Studying causing success is a result, not a contrast — use "so."

commonMistakes.wrong: Although it was raining, but we went for a walk.
commonMistakes.right: Although it was raining, we went for a walk.
commonMistakes.why: Don't combine "although" with "but" — the contrast is already built into "although."

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the best connector.

items.prompt: I like coffee, ___ I don't like tea.
items.explanation: A contrast between two preferences needs "but."

items.prompt: She studied hard, ___ she passed the exam.
items.explanation: Studying causes passing — a result, so "so."

items.prompt: I stayed home ___ I was sick.
He wanted to buy the car, ___ he didn't have enough money.
items.explanation: A contrast (wanted it, but couldn't) needs "but" or "however."

items.prompt: "___ it was raining, we went for a walk." — which word fits, without adding "but" later?
items.explanation: "Although" already contains the contrast, so no "but" is needed afterward.

items.prompt: She's very talented; ___, she doesn't have much experience.

items.incorrect: Although it was late, but we kept working.
answer: Although it was late, we kept working.
items.explanation: Don't combine "although" with "but" — the contrast is already built in.

items.incorrect: It was raining, so we stayed inside because we got wet.
answer: It was raining, so we stayed inside.
We got wet because it was raining.
items.explanation: "So" (result) and "because" (reason) shouldn't be mixed backwards in the same clause — keep cause and effect in a clear order.

summary: Addition: also, as well as, moreover. Contrast: but, however, although. Reason: because/since. Result: so/therefore.
Don't combine "although" (or "whereas") with "but" — the contrast is already built in.
"Because" introduces the cause; "so" introduces the effect — keep the order clear.
